cases.subtitle: Our people have been part of creating amazing projects.

legohouse.problem: LEGO House in Billund, Denmark, opened in 2017 with 30+ software experiences centered around the physical LEGO brick. The software was inadequate and had a negative impact on the guest experience: crashes and errors meant that customers often left disappointed. Play Agents, who were meant to facilitate a great experience, spent too much time mitigating technical issues and asking the IT department for assistance.
legohouse.solution: Experiences that were inadequately built had to be remade. By taking the software that worked, improving or replacing what didn't, LEGO House underwent a digital rebuild. With reliable software, Play Agents now have more time for guest interactions and fun. Connecting every experience to a shared platform, Play Agents are empowered to handle basic software and hardware failures themselves. At the touch of a button, using an iOS app, Play Agents can manage edge devices, saving hours daily. Guests and LEGO House are happier than ever.
legohouse.tech:
Most experiences had heavy emphasis on 3D graphics and the Unity game engine had great toolsets, fair pricing, already used within LEGO and supports a programming language we are really good at: C#.

The shared platform was written in C#/ASP.NET and at the center was an event-driven RabbitMQ service enabling guest-checkins via NFC, photo/video capture, observability, edge device interaction and automatic startup/shutdown power-savings.

Everything was hosted in Azure, using Container Apps, Blob storage, and MSSQL databases, except the on-device Unity instances.
